segments.text: Roll a dice. Is it a six? Just yes or no.
segments.caption: Roll a dice. Is it a six? Just yes or no.

segments.text: That simple question has its own distribution: Bernoulli.
segments.caption: That simple question has its own distribution: Bernoulli.

segments.text: And rolling until you finally get a six? That's the geometric distribution.
segments.caption: And rolling until you finally get a six? That's the geometric distribution.

segments.text: First, Bernoulli, in simple words.
segments.caption: First, Bernoulli, in simple words.

segments.text: A Bernoulli distribution is one try, with two outcomes: success or failure.
segments.caption: A Bernoulli distribution is one try, with two outcomes: success or failure.

segments.text: We write success as one, and failure as zero.
segments.caption: We write success as one, and failure as zero.

segments.text: And it needs just one number: the chance of success.
segments.caption: And it needs just one number: the chance of success.

segments.text: Roll once. A six is a success, with a chance of one in six.
segments.caption: Roll once. A six is a success, with a chance of one in six.

segments.text: Anything else is a failure: five in six.
segments.caption: Anything else is a failure: five in six.

segments.text: So the shape is just two bars: a tall one for zero, and a short one for one.
segments.caption: So the shape is just two bars: a tall one for zero, and a short one for one.

segments.text: Yes-or-no outcomes are everywhere in data science.
segments.caption: Yes-or-no outcomes are everywhere in data science.

segments.text: Did the customer click? Is this email spam? Will they buy?
segments.caption: Did the customer click? Is this email spam? Will they buy?

segments.text: Many machine learning models predict exactly this: the chance of a yes.
segments.caption: Many machine learning models predict exactly this: the chance of a yes.

segments.text: And repeat the try many times, counting the yeses? That's the binomial you've already seen.
segments.caption: And repeat the try many times, counting the yeses? That's the binomial you've already seen.

segments.text: Now, the geometric distribution.
segments.caption: Now, the geometric distribution.

segments.text: It counts how many tries it takes to get the first success.
segments.caption: It counts how many tries it takes to get the first success.

segments.text: Like the exponential, it's about waiting. But instead of measuring time, it counts tries.
segments.caption: Like the exponential, it's about waiting. But instead of measuring time, it counts tries.

segments.text: Keep rolling until you get a six.
segments.caption: Keep rolling until you get a six.

segments.text: A six on the very first roll? One in six, about seventeen percent.
segments.caption: A six on the very first roll? One in six, about 17%.

segments.text: On the second roll? About fourteen percent. On the third? About twelve.
segments.caption: On the second roll? About 14%. On the third? About 12.

segments.text: Each extra roll is a bit less likely, so the bars step down.
segments.caption: Each extra roll is a bit less likely, so the bars step down.

segments.text: Surprise: the single most likely roll is the very first one!
segments.caption: Surprise: the single most likely roll is the very first one!

segments.text: But on average, how long do you wait?
segments.caption: But on average, how long do you wait?

segments.text: One over the chance. With a one-in-six chance, that's six rolls.
segments.caption: One over the chance. With a one-in-six chance, that's six rolls.

segments.text: So remember: Bernoulli is one try, yes or no.
segments.caption: So remember: Bernoulli is one try, yes or no.

segments.text: Geometric counts the tries until the first yes. And the average wait is one over the chance.

segments.text: Quick quiz!

segments.text: A salesperson closes one call in every four.

segments.text: On average, how many calls until the first sale?

The average wait is one over the chance. A one-in-four chance means four calls.
